channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold slumps below $4,350 on higher US yields, hawkish Fed bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to near a two-week low around $4,330 during the early Asian session on Wednesday. The precious metal faces some selling pressure on elevated Treasury yields and a stronger US Dollar (USD).

item.title: RBNZ expected to hike interest rate amid sticky inflation
item.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is on track to deliver a follow-through interest rate hike, raising the Official Cash Rate (OCR) by another 25 basis points (bps) from 2.50% to 2.75% on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls as US-Iran conflict lifts USD, GDP data eyed
item.description: The Aussie Dollar retreats some 0.29% against the US Dollar on Tuesday as the escalation of the Middle East conflict boosted the Greenback due to its haven appeal. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7146.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Range-bound consolidation outlook against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann discuss recent volatility in USD/CNH after a sharp rebound and subsequent drop.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: 200-day SMA caps Euro as Dollar firms
item.description: The shared currency edges lower, capped by the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at 1.1633, amid rising geopolitical tensions and escalating hostilities between the US and Iran, prompting investors to buy the US Dollar. At the time of writing, the EUR/USD trades at 1.1590, down 0.25%.

item.title: India: Growth and inflation forecasts revised higher – UOB
item.description: UOB's Jester Koh note they raise their FY27 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) forecast for India to 7.2% from 6.8% after a stronger-than-expected 1QFY27 expansion of 7.8% year-on-year.

item.title: Asia FX: KRW and MYR lead firmer profile vs USD – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong have recalibrated Asian FX forecasts slightly firmer against the US Dollar (USD), with more notable upgrades for KRW and MYR.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Volatility widens range-trading band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD has retreated sharply after last week’s spike, but downside momentum remains limited.

item.title: Mexican Peso holds near 17.00 as US-Iran strikes weigh on Peso
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) erases some of its earlier gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as the US and Iran launched successive strikes against each other, souring risk appetite and weighing on the emerging market currency. The USD/MXN pair trades at 16.99, virtually unchanged.

item.title: India: Growth outlook revised higher – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered strategists Anubhuti Sahay and Saurav Anand revise their FY27 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth forecast to 7.2% from 6.6% following a robust Q1-FY27 print and strong high-frequency indicators.

item.title: Gold collapses as US-Iran strikes send Oil, US yields higher
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price collapses over 2.30% on Tuesday as the Middle East conflict escalates, with the US and Iran exchanging strikes, while US economic data was mixed but moved to the back seat amid geopolitical tensions.

item.title: China: Trade imbalances and weak demand – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists highlight growing pressure on China’s trade model as US-led restrictions target links with Iran and Venezuela.

item.title: Equities: Fragile advance under energy and yield risks – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) strategists note that global equities, including the MSCI ACWI, remain on track for another positive quarter, helped by an August rebound.

item.title: United States Treasury yields read Iran strikes as inflation
item.description: The 10-year Treasury yield trades near 4.79%, roughly four basis points higher and at its highest level since January 2025, in a fifth consecutive session of selling.

item.title: US Dollar Index gains as US-Iran tensions escalate, Treasury yields rise
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) edges higher on Tuesday, reversing all of the previous day’s losses as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations and rising US Treasury yields provide a strong tailwind.

item.title: Hungary: Growth strengthens but structural limits remain - ING
item.description: ING economists Peter Virovacz and Zoltán Homolya see Hungary on a gradual but constrained growth path after Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 0.5% QoQ and 1.7% YoY in the second quarter.

item.title: US President Trump says US striking Iranian targets near Hormuz
item.description: US President Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social account on Tuesday that the US is striking Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for Iran’s "failed attempt" to add sea mines in the Strait, which currently “has no mines.”

item.title: Forex Today: Enter the US labour market
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has managed to leave behind the negative start to the week and regained balance on Tuesday. The recovery has come on the back of a generalised recovery in US Treasury yields and ongoing tensions in the geopolitical landscape.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average finds no bid under confirmed strikes
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 52,750, roughly 450 points and 0.85% lower, at fresh session lows made after Central Command confirmed that American forces had begun striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets inside Iran.

item.title: Crude Oil goes vertical on fresh explosions in southern Iran
item.description: Crude Oil reached its session high in a straight line rather than a grind, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) pinned beneath $87.50 through the afternoon before taking better than a dollar and a quarter in three consecutive five-minute bars to print just short of $89.00.

item.title: Explosions in Iran renew Hormuz war fears – Iran International
item.description: Iran International reported on Tuesday explosions in Chabahar, Bandar Abbas and other Iranian cities near the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent backs Yen support, urges BoJ clarity
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that he emphasized the importance of sound formulation and communication of monetary policy to anchor inflation expectations in a meeting with Bank of Japan (BoJ) Governor Kazuo Ueda.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar struggles to rebound despite softer US data
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5900 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down 0.24% on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure against the US Dollar (USD), which holds onto modest gains despite the release of mixed United States (US) economic data.

item.title: Gold struggles below $4,400 as Fed rate hike bets dominate
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its pullback from the more-than-three-month high touched last week and falls to a fresh two-week low on Tuesday. Rising expectations of Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes and fresh tensions in the Middle East remain the main drivers behind the latest leg lower.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent backs Japan's steps, presses G20 on Iran
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that Japan is taking the right steps for its economy, and that G20 finance ministers want more growth.

item.title: Australian Dollar trades cautiously as Fed and RBA rate hike bets clash
item.description: AUD/USD trades with a modest downside bias on Tuesday as softer-than-expected United States (US) economic data fail to generate sustained selling pressure on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Germany: Coalition risks and reform hurdles – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Ralph Solveen analyzes how the Saxony-Anhalt election and two subsequent votes in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania could strain Germany’s CDU/CSU–SPD coalition.

item.title: British Pound stalls as mixed US data keeps Fed hawkish bets alive
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) trades sideways versus the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday after mixed US economic data, with manufacturing activity dipping in August, while a strong jobs market backs Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish tilt. The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3540, down a modest 0.06%.

item.title: United Kingdom: Growth cools as inflation risks build – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank economists Sanjay Raja and Maui Brennan say the UK enters autumn as the fastest-growing G7 economy, helped by strong ICT and AI-related investment and improving productivity.

item.title: Euro struggles as softer-than-expected US econoomic data offer little relief
item.description: EUR/USD struggles to attract buyers on Tuesday despite below-forecast US economic data, as the US Dollar (USD) shows little weakness following the release. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1601 after touching an intraday low of 1.1587, but remains down roughly 0.14% on the day.
